one_star_reviews.text:
If I could give Vetland zero stars I would.
Prince died on the 1/6/26 this year. It’s taken me a long time to write this review. His beds and toys are still in the same place he left them around our home.
I do not recommend this horrendous place for animals. They care only about how much money they can take.

Unfortunately, this was the first place that came up at 1am when I needed a vet. I’d seen the reviews and went with it. If you are reading this review, looking for a vet, go, run elsewhere.

Prince went in for surgery and was promptly sent home very early the next morning. Each day after his surgery, I returned with him deeply concerned. I was reassured all was well. He was not able to wee. His skin had turned red and I was told it was a mystery. Finally, a few days later after repeatedly returning, ringing they kept him overnight. I did not recognise him the final day. I was told he needed a feeding tube. He could barely walk and was just a mess. By this final stage, I certainly was not going to put him through any further pain.                       He had just turned 10. Here’s some photos of my beautiful Prince. The first two, a few days after his operation. The last two, how I’ll always remember him.

Vetland, don’t bother replying back to me with some passive aggressive nonsense. I wish I’d gone somewhere else. RIP my beautiful Prince.

Won’t recommend unless you are prepared to sign a contract instantly. They are very friendly until you don’t want to proceed. I said I tried calling but there is no direct number to Maroochydore showroom. The number I phoned said that they are open Monday to Friday business hours. Finally I received a phone call from Halena which she only to proceed to talk over me and said their phone number was on the voucher which Jane had ripped up.
Jane the designer told me that Halena gave me a discount on the appliances but Halena said she couldn’t give further discounts because that would be someone’s else’s decision. Who is telling the truth? Good old sales trick.
Halena kept speaking over me and wouldn’t let me speak and then she said we need to end this conversation. Which was fine by me because I don’t want to deal with a company that doesn’t want to listen to the clients. When I mentioned I had a private contractor who had given me the CAB design and if they could come down in price? Halena said that the materials would definitely not the same as ours. Since Halena didn’t let me speak my cabinets are Australian made, UV, 16mm thick and no pushing into signing a contract! Plus the same warranty Kitchen Connections offer.
Halena at The Maroochydore showroom was lovely at the first meeting but her attitude changed when I asked for the prices of the appliances and that I had already received another quote that included the CAB design which Jane used to make some modifications. Very helpful but I right at the end of the appointment I was informed that at the measurement and design stage, I would need to sign a contract there and then! They won’t give you a quote! You have to sign a contract. All companies that I have dealt with give free quotes. Plus when I think cabinetry it should include the front too not just the carcass. Misleading advertising. Be wary and that they expect you to sign that contract at the design.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1 star - Extremely disappointing experience with Amart Furniture Fyshwick

I honestly don’t like leaving negative reviews, but our experience with Amart Furniture Fyshwick has been so frustrating I feel it needs to be shared.

Early August, we purchased a couch from the Fyshwick store for nearly $3000. We were told the main part would take around 3–4 weeks, with my understanding the additional piece would take around 5–6 weeks.

Things started going wrong almost immediately.

I was told my receipt would be emailed, but it never arrived. I contacted customer service, provided another email address and still received nothing. I eventually had to chase it up again.

Almost two weeks later, I called for my receipt and an update. I was transferred to Fyshwick and spoke to the same staff member who sold us the couch.

I was told I had misunderstood the delivery timeframe and the ottoman was holding up the order. I said I was happy to have the couch delivered first and collect the ottoman separately, as it would fit in my car.

I was told the whole couch would be ready mid-September, but i could instead have the ottoman sent to the store for me to collect while the couch was delivered home earlier.

Great! Problem solved, or so I thought.

I was told I would receive a call the following week to organise delivery. I never did.

So today I contacted customer service again, only to be told the information from the store was incorrect. Only the corner piece was ready and the remainder wouldn't be available until late September/early October. I was also told there was no way the couch could have been delivered this week, despite what I had previously been told.

At this point, I asked for a refund.

I was transferred to Fyshwick and the gentleman I spoke to was immediately defensive. He told me the staff member's notes said "late September". I explained repeatedly this was not what I had been told, yet I felt like I was being called a liar because he said the notes said something different.

At one point he said:

"If you keep talking over me, I'm going to have to hang up on you, and I'm not going to answer your questions."

I wasn't calling to argue. I was trying to understand where my nearly $3000 purchase was, why I'd been given multiple timeframes and what my options were.

I was then told I had to physically go to the store for the refund because I needed to tap the original card. So I collected the card from my husband's workplace and drove to Fyshwick.

When I arrived, another staff member processed the refund. Then I was told, "And now just tap any card."

So apparently I didn't even need the original card.

That was the final straw for me.

I completely understand furniture delays and supply issues happen. What I don't accept is conflicting information, having to repeatedly chase basic updates, being told one thing by the salesperson and another by customer service, then being spoken to rudely when trying to resolve it.

The issue isn't just the delayed couch. It's the lack of communication, contradictory information, failure to follow through and the attitude I received.

Unfortunately, we won't be purchasing from Amart Fyshwick again. You have lost this purchase and we will be going to your competitors.

I hope management actually looks into what happened here.

Unfortunately our Girls Weekend at Lavender Majestic wasn’t what we believed we had booked.
The experience is advertised as having a “butler on site”, however what wasn’t clearly disclosed was that the male butler would actually stay and sleep inside the house with us for the entire weekend, in a fourth bedroom.
As a group of women booking a girls getaway, this is something we absolutely believe should have been made clear before booking and paying. “On site” and “residing inside the house overnight” are very different things.
The butler himself was lovely and did a great job, our complaint is not about him. It’s about transparency, privacy and being able to make an informed choice. We want to make it clear to other people looking that this is advertised everywhere as a GIRLS GETAWAY THIS IS WHAT IT IS!

We contacted the owners directly afterwards hoping to resolve our concerns, but unfortunately no resolution or compensation was offered.
For the amount we paid, this was really disappointing and significantly changed the experience for us. Future guests should be clearly informed of the living arrangements before they book.

Disappointing experience at Chemist Warehouse Coolangatta

This was my first time visiting the Coolangatta store, and unfortunately the customer service was quite disappointing compared with other Chemist Warehouse stores I’ve visited.

I came in specifically interested in the Bundle of Joy promotion, but I couldn’t find any signage in the store explaining the promotion or the minimum spend required.

I asked a staff member whether the promotion was running today. She said yes, so I then asked how much I needed to spend to receive the gift. She vaguely replied, “around $70.” She didn’t seem sure of the answer, but instead of checking, she simply walked away. I later checked online and found that the qualifying spend was actually $79.

I continued shopping and went to the checkout. Even when I was about to pay, the cashier didn’t mention the Bundle of Joy gift at all. I had to specifically ask, “Is there a Bundle of Joy?” She visibly hesitated for a moment, simply said “yes,” and only then went to get it for me.

The whole experience made me feel like customers were expected to already know about the promotion and specifically ask for the gift themselves, rather than staff proactively explaining or offering it.

I’ve visited many other Chemist Warehouse stores and have generally found the staff friendly and helpful, so this experience really stood out in comparison. I hope the Coolangatta store can improve its customer service and make promotional information clearer and more consistent for customers.

one_star_reviews.text:
We came to Champion Lake Vet Centre seeking advice and treatment options for our 2½-year-old bulldog’s cherry eye, and unfortunately walked away incredibly upset and angry with the experience.

Our dog had been on a walk immediately before the appointment and was only about three minutes into being seen when he was taken from us. We explained repeatedly that we know our dog, we know his breathing patterns after exercise, and that his breathing settles once he has had time to calm down. Despite us trying to communicate this, we felt completely unheard.

He was then sedated to the point that he could not even walk himself out of the vet. We have now left with him lying completely out of it in the back of our car, which is extremely distressing to see.

My biggest issue is the complete lack of listening to us as his owners. Knowing the general characteristics and potential risks associated with a breed does not mean every individual dog is exactly the same. Owners live with their animals every single day and know what is normal for them. When an owner is repeatedly trying to explain their dog’s normal behaviour and breathing, that information deserves to be listened to and taken seriously.

We came in wanting help and information about his cherry eye. Instead, we have left with no resolution to the reason we attended and a dog so heavily sedated he cannot walk, along with two owners who feel completely disregarded.

Please listen to owners. Clinical knowledge is obviously incredibly important, but so is listening to the people who know the individual animal standing in front of you. This entire experience has left us extremely disappointed and angry.

Very disappointing experience. I placed my order at 2:15 pm and specifically scheduled it for 4:50 pm, assuming that a scheduled order meant it would be ready at the selected time. However, when I arrived at 4:50 pm, I was still told to wait and didn’t receive my drinks until 5:10 pm.

If customers still have to wait another 20 minutes after the scheduled pickup time, then what is the point of offering scheduled orders in the first place? I ordered more than two and a half hours in advance, so there was plenty of notice to prepare the order on time.

What made the experience worse was the attitude of the staff member who was making the drinks at around 5:00 pm on Sunday, 23 August. I found their manner very unfriendly and dismissive, and there was little sense of apology or concern about the delay. When an order is already running significantly late, I would at least expect staff to communicate politely and professionally with customers.

I understand that stores can get busy, but if you offer customers the option to choose a specific pickup time, that time should actually mean something. Poor time management combined with poor customer service made this a very frustrating experience.

If no reasonable explanation, apology, or appropriate compensation is offered, I am prepared to pursue this matter through all available and appropriate consumer complaint channels, regardless of the time and effort involved.

Sharetea really needs to improve both its scheduled-order system and staff customer service.

Very disappointing experience

I took my 3-year-old daughter to see Dr Alex Coe regarding her eczema. He prescribed aZematop 0.1% (tacrolimus). After researching the medication and reading the Australian Product Information, I had concerns about the 0.1% strength being prescribed for a 3-year-old, so I contacted the clinic to understand the reasoning behind the prescription.

The receptionist contacted me instead of the doctor and, understandably, couldn’t answer my medical questions. I specifically requested a call from Dr Coe. I was told he would call, but the agreed time passed without a call. I was then told he was running late and would call “at the end of his consulting,” with no timeframe.

What disappointed me most was being told through the receptionist that if I wasn’t comfortable with the medication, I could simply use an over-the-counter alternative. That didn’t answer my question. I wasn’t asking for an alternative — I wanted the doctor to explain why he chose this particular medication and strength for my 3-year-old.

I completely understand doctors can run late, but when it concerns medication for a young child, I expect my questions to be properly addressed by the treating doctor.

I ultimately decided to seek a second opinion elsewhere. Very disappointing experience with the communication and follow-up.

Run! I flew interstate to a beautiful setting and was told I would have a lot of support. I was there not even 3 full days. I was very honest with my pre-existing medical conditions epilepsy, endometriosis as well as my mental heath issues, I had also explained what medicines were prescribed, they advised me they would be locked in a safe in the office, which they ended up giving to me to keep in my room as they couldn't manage them? Not good if I was an addict or suicidal. I arrived on the Thursday afternoon, unpacked and settled in. I went and met some of the staff and guests and interacted, on the Sunday morning I had a medical incident and was placed in an ambulance. While at the hospital they (Palladium Private's retreat manager) said that I faked my seizure, (how and why would I do that, not mention she is not medically trained) and were too complex for them amd literally said that "I was in the too hard basket" so wouldn't let me stay unless we paid $450 per day for a chaperone, when they had full disclosure prior to my admission and accepted the money I had to borrow from my parents. I had 1 session with a psychologist and 1 massage plus a couple meals and an excursion, as you don't have therapies over the weekend. One of the facilitators chose an inappropriate movie for the Saturday movie night that triggered quite a few people to the point a lot of us walked out. The way they handled the refund was appalling! Ended up costing roughly $6,000 for not even 3 FULL days & barely any treatment. Lucky I have a cousin in QLD so could stay there while I could figure out what I could do. The only good things were my massage, the setting, the food & the lovely lady who picked me up from hospital and drove me halfway to my cousins house. Very disappointed in the way this was handled, things that were said by the manager and the whole experience. I had committed to the program and invested my heart into getting 'me' back, as they promised they would help me to. I got the help I needed in Sydney that is similar & all covered by private health. Definitely don't recommend Palladium Private for your recovery. There should be at least 1 staff member on at night as people were drinking and doing drugs and were getting others involved. We ensured all contact thereafter was done via emails to keep a record.

EDIT; RESPONSE TO OWNER:
Thank you for responding, however, I have a few issues with your response. I gave the rating when I left but never actually wrote the review.
1. Your admissions were fully aware of all medications and medical conditions prior to accepting me into your program, they were given complete and accurate information.
2. I was fully aware of your program and had several very in-depth discussions with the lady who arranges admissions about both the program and the nature of it as well as information via email, otherwise I would not have handed over $20,000.
3. You have clearly disregarded those procedures as I was given a large quantity of Class A medications in my room, yet other guests had theirs given at a specific time. I remember "neighbour" needed medication management in the form of suboxone-which is a Class A drug.
4. You do offer on-going after hours care in the form of a chaperone at $450 per day, if I remember the amount correctly.
5. People were caught breaking the rules and were not suspended as you claim.
6. I had one risk assessment (it was a welcome how are you?) and that was when I arrived.
7. You did not address the serious misconduct by your staff, such as the inappropriate comments and unsolicited medical diagnoses made by a person not medically trained.
Again, thank you for your response. I am happy for those that you do help, however, for the money you got out of me I should have gotten a lot more assistance. I left Palladium Private thinking you are just about the money.
Another edit: in your response you are implying that I consumed illicit substances and alcohol which are both categorically untrue. Moreso, it falls under defamation and slander which I shall seek legal advice for all.

If I could give zero stars, I would.
This firm is related to Sunwise Constructions, who misappropriated my $7k deposit and still owe me $4k after two years.
If you check out their website it is a dodgy site for the USA (with a US contact number). Be VERY CAUTIOUS about engaging and paying deposits to this firm.

‼️‼️Extremely disappointing and heartbreaking experience. ‼️‼️

Our cat Fred had been staying at this clinic for 12 days while being treated for cryptococcosis. Unfortunately, he was not improving and we were advised that euthanasia may be the kindest option.

My dad signed the consent forms, but we were specifically told the vet would call us at 12pm the following day to let us know whether Fred had improved or whether we should come in to say goodbye. We received no call.

We arrived at approximately 2:45pm to see Fred, only to discover that he had already been euthanised at around 10am and picked up at 12pm. We were not contacted beforehand and were therefore denied the opportunity to say goodbye.

What followed was extremely upsetting. Staff initially took us to the wrong cat, then couldn’t locate Fred. We were eventually told he had been euthanised and asked if we wanted to see him, only to then be told they couldn’t find him. We were later told he had already been collected hours earlier.

We spent over two hours trying to understand what had happened. When we questioned the lack of communication, rather than receiving empathy and accountability, we were told the vet had been too busy to call.

We understand veterinary clinics get busy, but being busy is not an acceptable reason to fail to contact a family about the euthanasia of their beloved pet when they were specifically promised a call.

We trusted this clinic to do the right thing by Fred and our family during an incredibly difficult time. Sadly, that trust was completely broken. We expected basic communication, compassion and professionalism, and we did not receive it.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, our experience with Bribie Island Real Estate was nothing but negative. As someone who works in the real estate industry myself, I know this is not the standard of service tenants should expect.
From the beginning, there were countless issues. When we moved into the property, it had not been cleaned properly, which we noted on our entry condition report. We were also never provided with keys for the boundary fence or the garage which we had to chase up and still never provided with garage keys.
Throughout our tenancy, we repeatedly raised concerns with the agency, but very little was ever resolved. The most significant issue was being left without hot water for the final month of our lease, forcing us to have cold showers throughout winter.
Communication from the agency was consistently poor. We experienced delays with important documentation, including never receiving entry notices upon open homes and waking up to a cue of people at our door (which I had to send away myself), and phone conversations often felt unprofessional, with personal emotions seeming to affect the level of service we received.
There were also ongoing disturbances from neighbouring holiday rentals, with loud parties continuing into the early hours of the morning and police being called on multiple occasions. Despite raising these concerns, very little was done.
When we broke our lease, the exit inspection process felt unfair which now after reading previous reviews seems to follow how they normally mistreat their tenants. We left the property thoroughly clean (cleaner then when we moved in), yet the agency still appeared determined to find fault even after we went back and cleaned it thoroughly for a second time, we ended up just paying what we had to to get it over and done with.
To make matters worse, the property itself was handed over to us in poor condition. Paint was peeling from almost every wall and majority of the ceiling due to ongoing moisture and mould issues, which appeared to be the result of inadequate waterproofing.
Overall, our experience with Bribie Island Real Estate was extremely disappointing. I would NOT recommend doing business with this agency and am more than happy to have Bribie Island in my rear-view mirror.

Two weeks ago, I organised a rental delivery, with multiple emails exchanged to ensure everything was arranged and confirmed. The delivery was then formally confirmed multiple times, with the last confirmation yesterday (Monday) for this Friday.

Incredibly, today (Tuesday), upon my further email to follow up on further details for the delivery, I have been advised, "We can’t deliver anymore as we are moving, maybe try MR Rentals.” This was communicated just two days before the scheduled delivery, despite having had two weeks to advise us of any potential issue. Please note, the delivery was already meant to happen last week and rescheduled  last minute.

It is difficult to understand how a business can accept and confirm a booking while apparently being unaware that they are moving and will be unable to fulfil it. A business relocation is hardly an unforeseen, last-minute event.

The dismissive suggestion to simply “try MR Rentals” was equally unimpressive. There was no meaningful attempt to assist with alternative arrangements.

This demonstrates an unacceptable level of organisation, communication and reliability. If a business cannot honour a confirmed booking, particularly one arranged well in advance, customers should at the very least expect reasonable notice and professional communication.

Completely unreliable and exceptionally poorly handled. I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely abysmal customer service.

I ordered a Build-A-Bear from the Joondalup, Australia store from Ireland, as a gift for my godchild, who had been seriously unwell and in and out of hospital. I couldn't be there myself, so I was trying to do something special for him from the other side of the world.

When placing the order, I realised I'd entered the wrong email address. I immediately had my cousin contact the Joondalup store to correct it, and she was told that this had been sorted and that everything was confirmed for collection.

The collection date arrived and my cousin went into the store to collect the bear only to be told that the order had been cancelled.
Nobody contacted me. Nobody contacted my cousin. Despite the fact that the email issue had already been corrected with the store, I received absolutely no warning that there was a problem.

I contacted customer service to find out what had happened and was eventually told that the order had been flagged as fraudulent because it was placed from Ireland for collection in Australia.

I can understand a security system flagging an unusual international transaction. That's not really my issue. Things like that happen.
My issue is what happened afterwards.
I was told I could simply place the order again.

I questioned whether placing the exact same order again would just result in it being flagged and cancelled again. I was told yes it would, and that they couldn't manually override it.

So naturally I asked why are you telling me to place the same order again when you already know your system is going to cancel it?
There was no useful solution offered.

I then asked to speak to a manager because I wanted an actual explanation and, more importantly, a resolution. I also asked for the names of the people dealing with my complaint, as every response was simply signed off as "Build-A-Bear", which  they very clearly hide behind.
And then… nothing.

No manager contacted me. No meaningful explanation. No attempt to find a way to get the teddy to me or my cousin. No follow up whatsoever.

And the refund wasn't actually what I wanted. I wanted the teddy bear.
That was the entire reason I placed the order.
I eventually had to buy my godchild a bear from somewhere else.

I completely understand that fraud/security checks exist and that an order can occasionally be cancelled. What I don't understand is cancelling an order without notifying the customer, allowing someone to physically turn up to collect i without knowing it has been cancelled and to make matters worse it was an online exclusive to be picked up ao my cousin couldnt even buy it there and then for him. And telling me to place the exact same order again despite knowing it will be flagged again, and then ignoring their request to speak to a manager.

The original cancellation was frustrating.
The customer service afterwards was what made this experience completely unacceptable.

For a company whose entire brand is supposedly about creating special memories for people, the way this was handled was incredibly disappointing especially given the circumstances behind why I was trying so hard to get this particular teddy bear in the first place.

If i could gove less stars i would.
Not because a fraud check happened, but because when something went wrong, nobody seemed interested in actually fixing it or taking responsibility.

one_star_reviews.text:
**Extremely disappointing and inappropriate customer experience**

I visited Cue on **25 August 2026 at around 2:00pm** and left feeling extremely uncomfortable and insulted by the way I was spoken to.

The sales assistant repeatedly told me that, because of my body shape, I could apparently **“only wear wide-leg pants”** and that I needed to **hide the parts of my body I don’t like**. I found these comments completely inappropriate and deeply upsetting. A salesperson should be helping customers find clothes they feel confident and comfortable in—not telling them what parts of their body they should hide.

The assistant was also **insanely pushy**. I tried to leave multiple times, but instead of respecting that I had made my decision, I was repeatedly told to give it more time. When I eventually changed back into my regular clothes, she said, **“Oh, you’re just giving up now?”** That comment was incredibly condescending and made an already uncomfortable experience even worse.

I was also told that I simply needed to **go up a bigger size** and that nothing would ever fit my shape perfectly. There is absolutely nothing wrong with acknowledging that different cuts fit differently, but the way this was communicated was incredibly insensitive and made me feel as though my body was the problem.

I understand that sales assistants are there to make sales, but there is a huge difference between offering styling advice and making a customer feel pressured, judged and uncomfortable about their body.

I have never experienced customer service like this at a clothing store. I strongly encourage management to address how customers are being spoken to and the pressure being placed on them. **Customers should leave Cue feeling confident in their clothes—not ashamed of their bodies.**

**Visit:** 25/08/2026, approximately 2:00pm.

one_star_reviews.text:
Serious concerns about the authenticity of Arabian Oud products

I fell in love with Arabian Oud perfumes while travelling in the Middle East. Whenever I travel, or my partner travels, I buy genuine Arabian Oud fragrances for my collection, so I am very familiar with several of the scents.

I was surprised to find Arabian Oud stocked at a small suburban pharmacy in Melbourne. I called the pharmacy beforehand and was told that the products were genuine, air-freighted to preserve freshness, and sourced directly from Saudi Arabia.

I drove about an hour each way to inspect and smell several fragrances rather than purchasing online. I am glad I did.

I own and regularly wear approximately five of the Arabian Oud fragrances I tested in store. The products I smelled were materially different from the genuine fragrances I own, including significant differences in the scent profile and potency. I also noticed differences in the atomisers and what appeared to be inconsistencies between some box dates and the release dates of the fragrances.

These observations have left me with serious concerns about the authenticity and provenance of the Arabian Oud products being sold here.

I would recommend anyone considering purchasing Arabian Oud from this store verify the authenticity and supply source directly with Arabian Oud before purchasing.

I have also noticed similar concerns with other fragrance brands stocked here, and would recommend exercising caution and verifying authenticity before purchasing.

It was my first time at Lifehouse, and as a first-time visitor, you really don’t know what to expect. I assumed I would need to ask someone at the concierge desk for directions or information, especially since there are several concierge areas, including A, B, C and D.

I had seen a doctor at Clinic D. I also didn’t know that I could validate my parking ticket at any concierge desk, as some areas did not have clear signage saying, “Validate parking ticket here.”

To make a long story short, I went to Concierge B. I approached the Asian lady on the right-hand side of the B concierge and politely asked if I could validate my parking ticket there. I also asked if I needed to pay anything, as I thought I could make the payment through her.

Unfortunately, I felt that her response was quite sarcastic and unfriendly. As a first-time visitor, I was simply asking for help because I genuinely didn’t know how the process worked.

I hope that next time, staff can be a little more patient and welcoming when assisting people, especially those who may be unfamiliar with the facility. You never know what someone may already be going through in their personal life.

A little kindness, patience and respect can make a big difference. Customer service is about helping people feel comfortable and supported, especially when they are unsure of what to do.

I am very disappointed with the level of aftercare and communication I received following my surgery with Dr. Woo.

I had my surgery last week and, only a few days after the procedure, I was experiencing significant pain. I tried calling the clinic multiple times for assistance with pain management, but my calls went unanswered and were not returned.

What made the situation particularly frustrating was the lack of follow-up after surgery. When a patient is only days into their recovery and experiencing significant pain, I believe there should be a reliable way to contact the clinic and receive appropriate medical advice and support.

Throughout the entire process, I made sure that all my bills and payments were paid on time. As a patient, I fulfilled my responsibilities and expected the same level of professionalism, communication and care from the clinic, especially during the critical post-operative period.

My concern is not simply about obtaining medication; it is about being able to reach someone when experiencing significant pain after surgery and receiving appropriate guidance about what to do.

I hope Dr. Woo and the clinic take this feedback seriously and improve their post-operative follow-up and communication. Patients should feel supported after surgery, not left repeatedly calling for help when they are already dealing with pain and recovery.

I take my health and safety very seriously, and I will also be escalating my concerns through the appropriate health authorities and offices, including raising the matter with the relevant Health Minister’s office if necessary. I believe concerns regarding post-operative care and patient communication deserve to be properly heard and reviewed.

one_star_reviews.text:
After avoiding Qantas international for nearly 20 years, I decided to give them another chance. It will be my last.
The unfortunate string of events started with the routing. Unless you are flying to New Zealand from Adelaide, Qantas forces domestic transfers through other hubs, which is frustrating enough. However, despite paying full premium prices to book the entire journey through Qantas, they put me on a partner budget carrier for my domestic leg to Sydney.
Knowing this budget carrier's notorious record for delays, I tried to change my flight. What followed was a masterclass in poor customer service:
The Call Center: Overseas agents gave me completely conflicting information that resolved nothing.
The Airport Counter (Pre-departure): I made the physical effort to go to my local airport service desk. Two staff members, including a senior agent, explicitly assured me that if I showed up early on my departure day, they could shift me onto a domestic Qantas-operated flight. Trusting their word, I left.
Departure Day: When I arrived early as instructed, the airport staff flatly refused, stating the previous advice was completely wrong. Instead of trying to assist or apologize for their team's error, the agent acted in an arrogant manner, and tried to shift the blame onto me.
Now, I am sitting at the airport waiting on a delayed budget carrier flight, risking my international Qantas connection. Qantas has proved once again that their customer service culture is broken, lacking consistency and competency. Never again.

I bought a WOLL Diamond Lite pan specifically because it’s marketed as suitable for high-heat cooking. After normal, careful use — no metal utensils, no harsh scourers, never washed while hot — the pan developed permanent yellow discolouration around the edges.

When I contacted WOLL’s customer service, I was told this was likely caused by oil residue, and the warranty claim was declined. I provided proof of purchase and photos showing the pan had been well cared for, and asked what specific evidence pointed to misuse rather than a manufacturing or coating issue, but received no clarification and no further response.

If a pan marketed for high-heat cooking discolours from ordinary cooking with oil, that seems like a product limitation, not customer misuse — and I’d expect a warranty process to reflect that. I’m otherwise satisfied with how the pan performs, but the lack of a fair resolution or clear answer has left me unable to recommend WOLL’s customer support.

one_star_reviews.text:
I purchased a jacket from the Doncaster store on 30 July. As the item was out of stock, a staff member checked the system and advised that another store had one available. I asked whether it could be transferred to the Doncaster store for collection, but was advised that it would need to be posted to my home instead.

When the jacket arrived on 3 August, I was extremely disappointed. It was poorly presented, covered in dust, and had numerous small white fibres or particles all over it. I tried using a sticky roller twice to remove them, but it made little difference. Before sending this item to a customer, the person responsible should have asked themselves a simple question: "Would I be happy to wear this myself?"

I then called customer service on 1300 987 289. Unfortunately, they were unable to assist and simply advised me to take the jacket to my local store.

I visited the Doncaster store at approximately 10:55 am on 3 August. Rather than acknowledging the poor condition of the jacket or apologising for the inconvenience, an older staff member repeatedly defended it by saying, "It's just wool and should look like this." That completely missed the point. This was about the poor presentation and quality of the item I received, not the material itself.

What I expected was a sincere apology and an effort to resolve the issue, such as checking whether another store had a better-quality jacket available for exchange. Instead, I was left with no option but to request a refund, which she processed immediately. Even then, there was still no apology. The interaction ended with, "All done sir, thank you and goodbye!"

This entire experience—from receiving a jacket in unacceptable condition, to unhelpful customer service, to the dismissive attitude in-store—has been extremely disappointing.

Unfortunately, this is not the level of service I expect from an Australian brand. As a result of this experience, I will not be purchasing from Gazman again.

Unfortunately, I feel like I have no choice but to leave this review after getting no response from Bob Jane head office.

We've been to Bob Jane Essendon before for new tyres and a wheel alignment, and Paula has always been fantastic. That's why this experience was so disappointing.

Dad had a 2:30 pm appointment and arrived around 2:20 pm, but his car wasn't taken into the workshop until around 4:30 pm, with very little communication about the delay. After waiting more than two hours, the car was looked at for only a few minutes before Dad was told they couldn't do the wheel alignment because they couldn't loosen an adjustment nut and, because the car was "old", he would need to take it to a mechanic. It's a well-maintained 2011 Holden VE Series II with relatively low kilometres and a full service history. No wheel balancing was carried out or discussed either, so Dad left after more than two hours with nothing done.

The next morning, someone from Essendon called and said, "we need to sort this out for your dad" and offered to get the car back in. By then it was already booked at Bridgestone, who completed the wheel alignment that same day without any issue.

That's what I really wanted an explanation for. If the store had simply fallen behind and run out of time, I wish they had just told Dad. Delays happen and we would have understood. Instead, we were told there was an issue with the car that apparently prevented the work from being done, yet Bridgestone had no problem the next day.

I emailed head office on 27 July and followed up again on 12 August. I still haven't received a response. I would have much preferred to resolve this privately, especially given our previous positive experiences with the store, but unfortunately this is where we've ended up.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience - I would absolutely not recommend this salon.

I have never had such a frustrating experience with a hairdresser, and unfortunately, the way they handled my complaint afterwards was even more disappointing than the original service.

I went into the salon with a very clear idea of what I wanted. During my appointment, I actually raised concerns about the colour because it was already looking darker than I had asked for. The salon attempted to rectify this by re-toning my hair. I left with my hair styled in tight curls, so I could not properly see the final colour and result until I got home.

Once I was home and could see my hair properly, I was unhappy. The colour was completely different from what I had asked for and I did not feel that the result reflected what I had paid for.

I then emailed the salon on the same date, explained exactly what had happened and asked for a response as soon as possible given I was to go overseas at the end of that week. Despite knowing I was trying to resolve the issue urgently, I received no response until late afternoon three days later. By that point, another salon was able to respond promptly, understand the situation and fit me in to correct my hair.

I therefore had no choice but to pay another hairdresser to fix a service I had already paid for to get my hair to a standard I was originally expecting from the first salon.

I then contacted the original salon expecting them to take some responsibility and offer a reasonable resolution. Instead, I was told that because I had my hair fixed by another salon, they no longer needed to compensate me regardless of the fact that I contacted them in the first place to resolve the issue before I had to seek help from another hairdresser.

Not only is this against Australian Consumer Law, but it's also extremely disappointing. I had contacted the salon, given them an opportunity to respond and waited for them to do so. They did not respond within the timeframe I needed, leaving me to arrange and pay for the correction myself. I was then effectively told that because I had taken reasonable steps to fix the problem when the salon did not respond, I was no longer entitled to any compensation.

I also found the handling of my complaint extremely unprofessional. Rather than simply dealing with my concerns directly and professionally, other members of the salon were brought into the email correspondence. I found this unnecessary and inappropriate, particularly when I was attempting to resolve the matter privately and reasonably.

The biggest issue for me is the complete lack of accountability. I understand that mistakes happen. What separates a good business from a bad one is how they respond when something goes wrong. In my experience, this salon did not take responsibility for the outcome, did not respond with any urgency when I raised the issue, and ultimately left me to pay the financial and practical cost of fixing their service myself.

I have now had to escalate the matter to Fair Trading because I do not consider the salon's response to adequately address my consumer rights.

If you are considering booking here, I would seriously reconsider. I certainly will not be returning, and based on my experience, I would not recommend this salon to anyone looking for a professional, reliable and accountable hairdresser.

The most disappointing part is not simply that my hair was not done correctly. It is the way the salon handled the situation afterwards  - the delayed response, the lack of accountability and the fact that I was ultimately left to pay to fix the problem myself.

Photos attached show the reference photo I provided, my hair before the appointment (blonde with regrowth), and the result I was given. I was told the reference colour could be achieved and was never advised otherwise. Despite wanting to go lighter, I left with darker hair. I later went to another salon, who achieved the reference faster than I received a response from Blondes and Blowouts.

I am writing this review to warn other pet owners after a terrible and distressing experience at Greencross Vets Holden Hill.

I rushed my pet here in an emergency because he was extremely sick. The vet I saw, Lauren Fletcher, did not even bother to examine my pet initially. She simply relied on whatever information the receptionist, Tori, had written down. Without conducting a proper physical exam, she immediately scared me by saying that if I didn't perform a series of tests, X-rays, and surgeries right away, my pet would die. She randomly felt my pet’s belly and claimed he must have swallowed something hard, insisting on immediate X-rays and surgery.

What shocked me most was that she only took my pet out of his cage to check his body temperature AFTER I explicitly requested her to feel his body because he felt hot. Why did I have to tell a vet how to do a basic examination? To make matters worse, she sent my pet home without giving him ANY medication, claiming cats don't have many medication options, repeating that my pet would die without expensive procedures. Speaking to a distressed pet owner—who views their pet as a child—in such a blunt and alarming way is completely unacceptable.

The receptionist, TORI, made the experience even worse. She is extremely ill-mannered, rude, and aggressive when speaking to clients. She completely lacks basic empathy and professional courtesy, bringing personal attitude into her work. Pet owners coming in are already stressed and terrified; she needs to learn how to be gentle and respectful.

The ONLY reason I am giving any credit is to Dr. SARAH. When I returned a few days later, my pet was nearly passing away. Dr. Sarah treated him with genuine love, care, and compassion. She immediately administered the necessary medications to save his life and gave me the emotional support and reassurance I desperately needed.

Dr. Sarah is wonderful, but the treatment I received from Lauren Fletcher and Tori was traumatic, neglectful, and driven by scare tactics. Please be very careful if you take your beloved pets here.

This experience whole experience was a fever dream to say the least. Respectfully, if you want to shop at amart, please do yourself a favour and shop at another store where the staff actually behave appropriately. Or pop over to harvey norman next door and avoid this headache entirely.

Worth noting however that the delivery guys themselves were very good and work so hard.

Overall, excellent sales service, but a very disappointing property management experience. I would not recommend their property management services.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience with Samsung's warranty and complaint process.

I purchased a Galaxy Z Fold6 directly from Samsung as a premium flagship device. The inner display subsequently developed a serious failure along the folding area.

Samsung rejected my claim because the device had historical physical damage from an incident approximately 12 months earlier. I disclosed that damage and do not dispute its existence. What I dispute is Samsung's conclusion that the historical damage caused the much later inner-display failure.

I escalated the matter through Samsung's Customer Care and Voice of Customer teams. The process took approximately two months, during which Samsung retained my phone while I made numerous calls and sent multiple emails seeking updates. There were several promised callbacks and update timeframes that were not met, and at times I was unable to reach my assigned case managers.

Samsung has now provided its final position. Its explanation is that previous physical damage can cause microscopic internal damage that may deteriorate over time and eventually result in display failure. During my discussions with Samsung, I specifically asked whether its assessment established that the historical damage did actually cause the failure in my particular device, rather than simply being capable of causing such a failure. I was not given that confirmation.

Samsung has declined to provide a free repair or other remedy and instead quoted me $1,035 for the repair. I declined the paid repair and requested that my phone be returned unrepaired, together with copies of both technical assessment reports.

Regardless of the disagreement over causation, I expected considerably better durability and after-sales support from an expensive flagship device. The lengthy complaint process and repeated communication failures have made the experience particularly disappointing.

I will update this review if Samsung subsequently resolves the matter.

A couple of months ago, I had my earlobe pierced at SkinKandy and unfortunately ended up with an infection. Before getting the piercing, I purchased the premium earrings as well as the sterile aftercare spray they sell and recommend. I followed the aftercare instructions and used the spray twice a day as directed.

Despite following the recommended aftercare, the piercing became infected and I had to visit the doctor 2–3 times and purchase a $30 topical medication to treat it. This meant additional costs, time and a lot of unnecessary stress.

I contacted SkinKandy Customer Service to explain what had happened and was hoping they would show some understanding and offer a reasonable resolution. Instead, the Area Manager refused to offer another piercing and advised that it was outside of their liability because it had been a couple of months.

What I found particularly disappointing was that the Area Manager also addressed me by the wrong name in her email. This made me question how carefully my complaint and booking had actually been reviewed or investigated. When you are raising a health-related concern after an infection and multiple doctor visits, you expect your complaint to be taken seriously and handled with care and attention to detail.

I understand that infections can happen with piercings and that there are terms and conditions around liability. However, I had purchased the jewellery and recommended aftercare product directly from SkinKandy and followed the instructions I was given. I was disappointed by the lack of genuine concern or goodwill when I reached out for assistance.

For me, it wasn’t simply about getting another piercing. It was about the infection, multiple medical appointments, medication, the money I had already spent on the piercing, jewellery and aftercare products, and then feeling dismissed when I raised my concerns.

This experience has left me feeling that customer care was not a priority. I would strongly recommend considering your options carefully before getting a piercing here. In my experience, it wasn’t worth the additional cost, time, stress and risk of dealing with an infection and multiple medical visits.

⭐ 1/5 — An absolutely disgraceful experience.

I came to Grampians Health's Adult Acute Mental Health Unit in Ballarat expecting professional treatment, compassion and support. Instead, my experience has left me feeling intimidated, humiliated, unheard and, at times, genuinely unsafe.

The irony of a mental health facility contributing to the very distress it is supposed to treat is beyond disappointing.

I've experienced repeated restrictions on my freedom, distressing interactions with staff, concerns about searches of my personal belongings, and warnings about forced medication that I found deeply intimidating.

Even something as simple as attending an eye appointment across the road has become an unnecessary battle.

I've cooperated with treatment, acknowledged my mistakes, apologised when appropriate and repeatedly attempted to resolve concerns respectfully. Yet I've often felt that my concerns are treated as problems to be managed rather than complaints deserving genuine consideration.

To be fair, some staff have been genuinely compassionate and professional. Unfortunately, their efforts are overshadowed by experiences that have left me questioning the culture, accountability and leadership of this unit.

Being a compulsory mental health patient does not mean surrendering your dignity, your voice or your legal rights.

Patients should never feel afraid to question decisions, raise concerns or advocate for themselves.

Grampians Health needs serious reflection, greater transparency and genuine accountability. Mental health patients are vulnerable people seeking care, not inconveniences to be controlled.

I came here seeking help for my mental health. I never imagined I would have to fight this hard to protect my dignity while receiving it.

One star. And even that feels generous.

I was at Sunshine Coast Airport and happened to witness an exchange at the Europcar counter between a staff member named Krystal and a woman who had two small children with her. I was sitting outside the office

I don’t normally leave reviews about situations that don’t directly involve me, however after witnessing this interaction I felt compelled to share what I personally observed.

The woman was clearly upset and frustrated about the situation with her booking, but throughout the exchange I did not see or hear her verbally abuse Krystal or call her names. What I did witness was an incredible lack of compassion, understanding or genuine willingness to help from Krystal.

From an outside perspective, Krystal came across as completely disengaged and uninterested in finding any way to assist the customer. Her attitude gave me the impression that she simply did not care about the customer’s situation or the level of service she was providing. There was no warmth, empathy or attempt to make an already stressful situation any easier for a mother travelling with two very young children. I found the standard of service appalling.

I was particularly surprised to later see a review describing what appears to be the same incident and portraying the customer as “horrible” and abusive. That account does not reflect what I personally witnessed.

I did happen to see the customer again following the incident and was glad to hear that the matter had been escalated to Europcar Head Office. Given what I personally witnessed, I believe it was absolutely appropriate for the situation to be brought to their attention.

Regardless of whether there was an issue with the booking requirements, customers should still be treated with courtesy, patience and respect. As an independent witness, I felt it was important to share what I observed, as the level of customer service displayed was extremely disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing experience and a serious lack of transparency around pricing.

I booked a colouring service online that was advertised at under $300 and then had a consultation over the phone with the stylist, where we discussed what I wanted. I naturally have brunette hair, and the service was simply retouching my brunette colour and adding a few highlights — this was not a major blonde transformation or colour correction.

When I arrived at the salon, I was suddenly quoted $550 — more than double the price of the service I had booked online. I was then told that the stylist was apparently supposed to have quoted me $450 during the phone consultation, which she had not done. Even that amount is substantially higher than the service I had booked.

I completely understand that pricing can vary depending on hair length and the work required, but going from under $300 online to $550 after I had already had a consultation and arrived for my appointment is simply not reasonable.

There needs to be far more transparency around pricing. If the online booking price isn’t a realistic indication of what a customer will actually pay, that needs to be communicated clearly before they book — especially when a consultation has already taken place.

In the end, I walked out without having the service done, and the whole experience was a complete waste of my morning. Had the actual price been communicated to me during the phone consultation, I could have made that decision beforehand and saved myself the time and inconvenience of going to the salon.

Consumers deserve clear and upfront pricing so they can make an informed decision before committing their time to an appointment. I left feeling extremely disappointed and misled.
